record.original_question: For a labeling λ of the edges of the complete graph Kₙ by distinct integers 1, 2, …, (n choose 2), let l(λ) be the length of the longest simple path whose edge labels increase along the path, and let f(n) = min_λ l(λ). Determine the asymptotic behavior of f(n), including whether f(n) = o(n) and whether there exists ε > 0 such that f(n) > n^(1/2 + ε).

evidence.quote: Given a labeling λ: E(Kₙ) → {1, 2, …, (n choose 2)} of the edges of Kₙ with distinct integers, denote by l(λ) the length of a longest simple path with increasing labels. Determine f(n) = min_λ l(λ). ... Is f(n) = o(n)? Is f(n) > n^(1/2)+ε for some ε > 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $K_n$ denote the complete graph on $n$ vertices, and let $E(K_n)$ be its edge set, of size $\binom{n}{2}$. An edge-labeling of $K_n$ is a bijection $\lambda \colon E(K_n) \to \{1,2,\dots,\binom{n}{2}\}$. A simple path $v_0 v_1 \cdots v_k$ in $K_n$ is called increasing (with respect to $\lambda$) if $\lambda(v_0 v_1) < \lambda(v_1 v_2) < \cdots < \lambda(v_{k-1} v_k)$. Let $\ell(\lambda)$ denote the maximum number of edges in an increasing simple path under $\lambda$, and define
$$ f(n) = \min_{\lambda} \ell(\lambda), $$
where the minimum ranges over all such bijective edge-labelings of $K_n$.

Determine the asymptotic behavior of $f(n)$ as $n \to \infty$. In particular:
(a) Is it true that $f(n) = o(n)$?
(b) Does there exist $\varepsilon > 0$ such that $f(n) > n^{1/2 + \varepsilon}$ for all sufficiently large $n$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Chvátal and Komlós (1971), remains open in its full form. The current best lower bound, due to Bucić, Kwan, Pokrovskiy, Sudakov, Tran and Wagner (Israel J. Math. 2020), is f(n) ≥ n^{1-o(1)}, which positively answers part (b) (any ε ∈ (0, 1/2) works for large n). However, it is still unknown whether f(n) is linear in n or whether f(n) = o(n); the prevailing conjecture is that f(n) is of linear order, but this has not been established.

status_evidence.title: Nearly-linear monotone paths in edge-ordered graphs
status_evidence.snippet: The prevailing conjecture is that one can always find a monotone path of linear length, but until now the best known lower bound was n^{2/3-o(1)}. In this paper we almost close this gap, proving that any edge-ordering of the complete graph contains a monotone path of length n^{1-o(1)}.
status_evidence.claim: Best known lower bound is f(n) ≥ n^{1-o(1)}; whether f(n) is linear remains open.

status_evidence.title: Increasing paths in ordered graphs (West)
status_evidence.snippet: Graham and Kleitman proved f(K_n) ≥ √n − 3/4 − 1/2 and Calderbank, Chung, Sturtevant proved f(K_n) ≤ (1/2 + o(1)) n.
status_evidence.claim: Classical bounds: √n lower bound and (1/2+o(1))n upper bound.
